title: The golden lion, deeper
hook: Fazang's teaching: the gold and the lion's shape are one

segments.voice: Yesterday, interpenetration: each thing holding all things. Your line was without obstruction. Did two lamps share a room for you? Today we close the week with Fazang's lion. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

A wedding ring. A family's old one, maybe, handed down. One day it's too small, so a jeweler melts it and makes it into something new. A pendant. Is the ring gone? The shape is gone. Nobody can wear it on a finger anymore. But not one grain of the gold has gone anywhere. It's hanging around somebody's neck. Earlier on this path we met Fazang's golden lion, the statue he used to teach an empress. We heard the basic idea: the gold, the lion's shape, not two. Today we go back for a deeper look. The golden lion.
screen: `A RING, MELTED.` → `THE SHAPE IS GONE. THE GOLD ISN'T.` → `BACK TO FAZANG'S LION.`

segments.voice: First, the craftsman. In Fazang's essay, the lion doesn't make itself. It appears because a skilled worker shapes the gold. The lion depends on conditions: gold, a hand, a moment. So the lion has no lion-ness of its own. That's emptiness, the same thing the Tiantai fist showed us earlier this week. Second, the gold doesn't change. When the lion is made, the gold doesn't gain anything. When the lion is melted down, the gold doesn't lose anything. Fazang uses that to point at the deep nature of things, which isn't added to when a thing arises or taken away when it ends. Third, looking two ways. When you look at the lion, the essay says, there's only lion; the gold doesn't show. When you look at the gold, there's only gold; the lion doesn't show. And when you see both at once, both are fully there, hidden and shown together. That is principle and event without obstruction, yesterday's teaching, made into a statue. Fourth, every part. The lion's eye is gold, and so is its ear, and so is every hair. And because each part is gold through and through, Fazang says each part holds the whole lion. One hair, the whole beast. Now look back across the week. Tiantai's three truths, seeing one thing as empty, real and the middle. Zhiyi's stopping and seeing. Huayan's garland, its lamps that don't crowd each other out, and this lion. Two Chinese schools, two summits, and the same patient work: looking at an ordinary thing until the whole of the teaching shows through it.
screen: `THE CRAFTSMAN SHAPES THE GOLD.` · `MELTED OR MADE, THE GOLD IS THE SAME.` · `SEE THE LION, OR SEE THE GOLD.` · `EACH HAIR HOLDS THE WHOLE LION.` · then, large: `GOLD AND LION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look at an object's material and form. Choose something nearby: a wooden spoon, a clay bowl, a metal key. Hold it, or set it where your eyes can rest on it. Name its form once, quietly: spoon. Then follow the material back. The wood was a branch, and before that a tree drinking rain. Then follow it forward. One day the spoon will crack or burn, and the wood will become something else. A few breaths with each. Then come back to the thing in your hand, here, now, wood shaped as a spoon. If the mind drifts, return to the weight of it. The bell holds the time.
The golden lion. Fazang's teaching image: the gold and the lion's shape are one, and each part of the lion holds the whole. Today's word.
Your line: gold and lion. Today, when something you love changes shape, look for the gold that didn't go anywhere. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Students of the Huayan tradition read Fazang's Essay on the Golden Lion as a short introduction to the school's teaching, contemplating the relation of the gold (principle) and the lion (event).

fork.setup: you're looking at the golden lion. Fazang asks: when you see only the lion, where is the gold?
options: gone, until the lion is melted.

original.note: Chinese Jin shizi zhang: the Essay on the Golden Lion, attributed to Fazang.

trapdoor: what you thought: a golden statue of a lion.
what it means: Fazang's image for how the deep nature of things (the gold) and particular things (the lion) are one.

what a scholar hears: an essay that packs Huayan into one statue: dependent arising through the craftsman, the gold unchanged by making or melting, hidden and shown together, and each hair holding the whole.

sources.ref: the craftsman, the unchanging gold, seeing lion or gold, each hair containing the whole lion
sources.work: Fazang, Essay on the Golden Lion (Jin shizi zhang)

notes: Editor pass: practice reworked to follow the material back and forward in time, so it no longer repeats the 'one view, then the other, then both' pattern of day 1333's practice; mug swapped out (cups recur this week).
Week end (1331–1337): looks back at Tiantai, three truths, zhiguan, Huayan and interpenetration.

Fazang's essay paraphrased throughout; confirm that the craftsman, the gold unchanged by arising and ceasing, the hidden/manifest pairing and each hair containing the whole lion fairly render its sections.
Builds on year 3 day 985 (The golden lion), which introduced Fazang, Empress Wu and the mirrors; this day avoids the mirrors and the empress story beyond a one-line recall.
The ring image is the writer's illustration.
